title: Celestial fix: cedar-solve plate solving on real star images, then position from star elevations above an IMU vertical
summary: Runs cedar-solve (tetra3 API, v0.6.0 on NumPy 2) lost-in-space on 40 real SkyView Mellinger cutouts with a known WCS (12 and 20 deg FOV, random pointing and roll) and on the 20 real camera frames shipped with cedar-solve, reporting solve rate, pointing/roll error against the WCS and runtime on an M2 Max. A stdlib Marcq St Hilaire least-squares solver turns star elevations above the gravity vertical into latitude/longitude; a Skyfield-truth Monte Carlo sweeps level bias, vibration, accelerometer bias, clock error, refraction and FOV, and confirms 1 arcmin of level error = about 1.85 km. The 8 ESA tetra3 frames (mount alt/az in the file names) give a crude real-data fix.
verified: ran on 2026-11-06 with Python 3.12.14 (numpy 2.5.4, cedar-solve git tag v0.6.0 installed --no-deps, skyfield 1.55, astropy 8.0.2) on an Apple M2 Max: plate_solve_eval.py with and without --fov-hint, esa_mount_fix.py, position_fix_sim.py --runs 200; outputs in results/ and quoted in the README. Plate solving uses real images (SkyView Mellinger mosaic cutouts, reference = requested WCS; cedar-solve test frames, no reference). The position-fix budget is simulation with Skyfield truth; centroid noise, vibration and bias levels are stated assumptions. The ESA-frame position has no ground truth (capture site undocumented). 11 unittest tests pass in the venv; with plain Homebrew python3 10 pass and the Skyfield test skips. A planted Jacobian sign flip fails 4 tests. No real IMU, moving camera, lens distortion, ESA tetra3, Cedar-Detect or database generation was run.
shows: cedar-solve lost-in-space on real star images vs a known WCS, then lat/lon from star elevations above an IMU vertical; error budget for level, vibration, accel bias, clock, refraction
runtime: fetch ~5 min (~190 MB); plate solve ~10 s; sim ~5 s
key_result: [Plate solve](README.md#1a-accuracy-against-a-known-wcs): 40/40 real cutouts solved, pointing 5.2 arcsec median (12 deg FOV), ~30 ms per 1 MP frame; [position](README.md#error-budget-ran-2026-11-06---runs-200): 1 arcmin level = 1.85-1.87 km, 1 mg accel bias = 6.4 km, 1 s clock = 0.3 km at 50 N
